failure_summary.description: Two flight dates were put in one departure_date list, or a search_flights call was nested inside another. Invalid kwargs such as num_people and return_flights were also passed. No variable assignment or save_to_cache followed.
First searches were emitted as bare calls (search_flights(...), search_attractions(...)) with no variable and no save_to_cache. This overlaps with the flight and state failures.
The agent asked for a city the user had already named (halal restaurant in St. Louis). It also put a state abbreviation (AZ) into city= instead of state=.
A cuisine and rating request with 'near the hotel' was sent to filter_hotels(cuisine=...). The gold flow is search_restaurants followed by search_nearest.

For 'affordable under 325' the agent re-applied the old time filter to the unfiltered departure key. It skipped budget and the return leg. In another case it re-searched a domain that was already cached while the other domain's dates arrived.

patch.reasoning: Round-trip flight requests, bare un-saved calls and wrong parameter mapping caused most of the failures. Rule 9 already covers round trips, but the agent kept collapsing the legs or nesting calls, so a hard template with explicit prohibitions and trigger phrases is added. A compact argument-extraction rule covers the over-seeking and state-vs-city errors. A cross-domain routing rule covers restaurants near a hotel via search_nearest. A flight and refinement chaining rule covers budget filtering on the most refined key of each leg, and not re-searching cached domains.

edits.content:
## Rule 15: Round-trip / date-pair flight template and mandatory assign+save
- Trigger: a flight request with two dates ('leave May 17 and return May 21', 'May 16, 2025 to May 25, 2025', 'around May 21 possibly and returning May 28', 'round-trip'). Words like 'around' or 'possibly' still make the dates concrete, so never seek_information for them. Output exactly this shape:
  `departure_flights = search_flights(start_airport_city="A", end_airport_city="B", departure_date=["<date1>"])`
  `save_to_cache(key="departure_flights", value=departure_flights)`
  `return_flights = search_flights(start_airport_city="B", end_airport_city="A", departure_date=["<date2>"])`
  `save_to_cache(key="return_flights", value=return_flights)`
- NEVER put both dates in one departure_date list. NEVER nest one search_flights call inside another. NEVER pass return_flights, return_date or num_people (party size is not a flight parameter, so omit it) to search_flights.
- An airport code the user mentions ('I normally fly from LAS') becomes start_airport="LAS" on the outbound leg and end_airport="LAS" on the return leg, in addition to the city args.
- Every search_*, filter_*, sort_results and search_nearest call must be assigned to a variable and saved with save_to_cache. A bare `search_flights(...)` or `search_attractions(...)` line is always wrong, even for a first search.

## Rule 16: Extract arguments from the whole conversation before asking; map location and dietary words correctly
- Before writing seek_information, scan EVERY user turn for each mandatory arg. A city named anywhere (e.g. 'a halal restaurant in St. Louis') satisfies search_restaurants and search_hotels, so search immediately. Only a truly absent mandatory arg justifies seek_information.
- Dietary words map to restaurant flags in the same call: halal -> has_halal_options=True, vegan -> has_vegan_options=True, vegetarian -> has_vegetarian_options=True, gluten-free -> has_gluten_free_options=True, kosher -> has_kosher_options=True. Then save_to_cache(key="restaurants", ...).
- A US state name or 2-letter abbreviation ('AZ', 'Texas') goes in state="AZ" for search_attractions/filter_attractions, never in city=. Use city= only for actual cities. A stated attraction type goes in type=["Guided"], and the result is saved under "attractions".
- Hotel star ratings are a [min, max] pair: 'a 2 star hotel' -> stars=[2, 2]. A single number for a plain rating is [X, X].

## Rule 17: A new domain in a follow-up turn is a fresh search; 'near the hotel' means search_nearest
- If the last turn brings restaurant constraints (cuisine, restaurant rating, dietary needs) and the CACHE has no restaurants key, NEVER call filter_hotels with them (filter_hotels has no cuisine param and raises a validation error). Run `restaurants = search_restaurants(city=<city from the hotel search in the cache summary>, cuisine=[...], rating=[X, X])` and `save_to_cache(key="restaurants", value=restaurants)`.
- If the user also says 'near the hotel' (or near an attraction), additionally load the most refined hotels key with `h = get_results_from_cache(key="<latest hotels key>")`, then `nearest_restaurants = search_nearest(hotels=h, restaurants=restaurants, groupBy="restaurant")` and `save_to_cache(key="nearest_restaurants", value=nearest_restaurants)`. Use groupBy="hotel" when the grouping is by hotel. For attractions use search_nearest(hotels=..., attractions=..., groupBy=...) in the same way.
- Before using any kwarg, check that it exists in that specific tool's arg list in TOOL CONFIG. Never borrow a param from another domain's tool.

## Rule 18: Chain flight refinements per leg from the most refined key; don't repeat applied filters or re-search cached domains
- When the CACHE has filtered_departure_flights / filtered_return_flights (or other filtered_* flight keys), load THOSE for the next flight constraint, not the raw departure_flights/return_flights. Do not re-apply a filter (e.g. departure_time) that the cache summary already lists as 'Additionally filtering for ...'.
- 'Not particularly, just something affordable under 325' (or 'under $325', 'budget of 325') -> budget=325 only, with no time, class or airline params. Apply it to EACH flight leg with its own load, filter and save, e.g. `a = get_results_from_cache(key="filtered_departure_flights")`, `a2 = filter_flights(prior_results=a, budget=325)`, `save_to_cache(key="filtered_budget_departure_flights", value=a2)`, then the same for the return leg under a new key. A 'no other preference' reply that still contains a price cap is a new constraint.
- Time strings, if a time filter is really new, use the 12-hour style `"12:00 PM"` / `"5:00 PM"`. The `"12:00:00"` style raises 'Unrecognized time format' in filter_flights.
- When the last turn supplies the missing dates for one domain (e.g. hotel check-in/out) and another domain (e.g. attractions) already has a cache key, call ONLY the newly completed search (search_hotels with all stated hotel details such as num_people, budget, stars). Do not re-run the cached domain's search.
